inputs.original_text: SSANU’s one-month ultimatum over the 2009 agreement is a warning that years of unresolved commitments can bring universities to a standstill. But an indefinite nationwide strike would punish students and families as well as put pressure on government. The authorities should negotiate in good faith and honor legitimate obligations; unions, in turn, should recognize that shutting down education is not a cost-free way to make their case. Institutions need dependable staff and responsible leadership—not a cycle of promises and disruption.
inputs.modified_text: SSANU’s one-month ultimatum over the 2009 agreement should not become a license to hold students and families hostage through an indefinite nationwide strike. Government must meet legitimate obligations and negotiate seriously, but unions also have a duty to the public and to the next generation. Education is too important to be repeatedly disrupted by labor disputes. We need responsible leadership, reliable staff, and a culture that honors commitments without making students pay the price.
